verdict.rationale: Mastra ships its own official TypeScript packages that developers import directly, such as `createTool` from `@mastra/core/tools` and `createWorkflow`, and those packages include embedded docs that AI agents can read from node_modules. The evidence covers only a single TypeScript framework, however: it shows no separate client SDKs, no multi-language SDKs, and no OpenAPI spec (all probed paths returned 404), so coverage of "official SDKs" is partial. missing for 10: official SDKs beyond TypeScript, a documented client SDK for calling deployed Mastra servers, an OpenAPI spec to generate SDKs from, and independent hands-on corroboration of SDK breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI agents and applications.
Import `createTool` from `@mastra/core/tools` and define a tool with an `id`, `description`, `inputSchema`, `outputSchema`, and `execute` function.

Mastra packages come with embedded documentation in `dist/docs`. When you install a Mastra package, your AI agent can read these files directly from `node_modules` to understand the package's APIs and patterns.
